19.t: Working with data: current around a circuit
q: State the current at A1 with a 6 V supply.
Describe what the readings show about current in a series circuit.
The current is the same at every point (within small meter errors).
Identify the anomalous reading and suggest a cause.
0.13 A at A3 (9 V). Perhaps a loose connection, a misread scale, or a faulty ammeter.
Doubling the voltage from 3 V to 6 V did not double the current. Suggest why.
The lamps’ filaments get hotter at higher current, so their resistance increases; the current rises less than expected.
